newsitem.title: USA: Calif. steps up probe of Prudential Insurance Co.
newsitem.headline: Calif. steps up probe of Prudential Insurance Co.

text.p: California Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush said Thursday his department issued subpoenas as part of a stepped up investigation of Prudential Insurance Co's practices.

Quackenbush said in a statement his department would form a special investigative task force as part of the probe, adding he was seeking to suspend Prudential's license in the state if "they do not fairly and adequately compensate" hundreds of thousands of policyholders.

"While Prudential's unethical practices have been under review by my department for the past 18 months, the progress of discussions with Prudential about this matter convinces me that we need to finalize our case against Prudential as soon as possible," Quackenbush said.

"Consequently, today I issued the first of several forthcoming subpoenas and have formed a special task force of investigators and attorneys to develop the final pieces of evidence necessary to suspend Prudential's license," he said.
In June 1995, California joined several other states in a multi-state examination of Prudential Insurance.

The examination revealed that, from the early 1980s to the early 1990s, Prudential insurance agents used omissions, misrepresentations and forgeries to sell life insurance policies to policyholders, Quackenbush said.

As a result of these findings, the multi-state task force and Prudential proposed a settlement under the terms of which Prudential would pay a $35 million fine and implement a nationwide plan to compensate policyholders.
California's Department of Insurance rejected the proposed settlement. The department said it believed the settlement did not provide fair and equitable relief to policyholders.
